test_title: PYST 27: SSC MTS - Reasoning (Held on: 15 July 2022 Shift 2)
subject: reasoning
question: Marks obtained by the seven students of a tuition class, P, Q, R, S, T, U and V, are mentioned. P scored second highest marks in the class. Marks scored by V were more than only one of the persons. S's score was more than T but less than P. Three people got higher than T and three got lesser than T. Neither R nor Q received the lowest marks. Given that no two students have the same marks, whose marks were the lowest?
solution:
The pattern followed here is:

**Given:- **Marks obtained by the seven students of a tuition class, P, Q, R, S, T, U, and V, are mentioned.

1) P scored the second highest marks in the class.

2) Marks scored by V were more than only one of the persons.

⇒ _ > P > _ > _ > _ > V > _ 

3) S's score was more than T but less than P.

4) Three people got higher than T and three got lesser than T.

(It means T is scored middle of the class)

⇒ _ > P > S > T > _ > V > _ 

5) Neither R nor Q received the lowest marks.

(It means U scored the lowest marks on the tuition test)

⇒ _ > P > S > T > _ > V > U 

The position of R and U is not cleared from the above-given information. 

R/Q > P > S > T > R/Q > V > U 

Clearly, U scored the lowest marks.

Hence, the correct answer is **"U".**
